interpretation: The original 60-unit selection is now outcome-complete without deleting or numerically coercing the three organization units.

The person-only 57-unit secondary analysis shows very high later Major attainment (53/57), but baseline-adjusted advancement is much lower (24/57), illustrating that the list frequently selected people who were already established leaders.
Field differences are substantial: politics had the highest person advancement rate (80%), while pop culture had only 20% because every selected person was already scope3 at T0.
The science-tech field provides the clearest example of anti-inflation coding: later honors for pre-existing field-defining work do not count as new advancement.
Organization outcomes are trajectories rather than person career scores: NHN branched, ABEEK expanded institutionally, and CCEJ sustained broad national activity.
guardrails: Do not call 53/57 a 60-unit success rate.
Do not add organization trajectories to person Major/Apex/Advanced numerators.
Do not compare raw field rates as outlet performance; all six fields come from one parent project and have different baseline distributions and domain-specific ceilings.
Do not integrate all field secondaries into the common cross-media placement master without an explicit parent-project weighting/version policy.
